claims.statement: Polish businesses must already receive invoices through KSeF and most taxpayers have had to issue through it since 1 April 2026; rejected, missing, or mishandled invoices create paid bookkeeping rework and payment-delay risk.
The likely payer is an accounting office or SME finance owner using its bookkeeping, integration, or compliance budget; willingness to pay remains unverified.
A launch can use customer-granted KSeF credentials and documented exception workflows, but no customer authorization or accounting-office distribution agreement is currently held.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Accounting-office owner or SME finance lead; unverified
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: Generic accounting suites can absorb basic KSeF handling; defensibility must come from cross-client exception resolution and response-time evidence
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with accounting offices
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Direct outreach to Polish accounting offices and ERP implementers

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Assumption: 1,000-3,000 PLN per accounting-office customer through targeted outbound and partner referrals; unknown until tested
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Assumption: setup fee upfront and subscription monthly in advance
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Assumption: 65-80% after cloud and exception support at 10-30 offices; unproven
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Assumption: 4-10 hours onboarding plus 1-3 hours monthly support per office
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Data-processing agreements, security review, professional liability, and Polish tax-process review; exact cost unknown
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Per accounting office plus invoice-volume tier
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: API hosting, monitoring, document processing, and human escalation

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: Accounting software vendors add stronger exception dashboards or bundle support
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: Current paid bookkeeper time resolving KSeF exceptions, retrieving invoices, and reconciling failures; delayed invoice handling can defer payment or VAT workflow
commercial_mechanics.payer: Accounting office or SME finance function
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: Repeated KSeF exceptions after mandatory adoption or inability to monitor multiple clients efficiently
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: Monthly continuation if exception backlog and handling time remain measurably lower

contrary_evidence: The Ministry provides free KSeF applications, reducing willingness to pay for basic access.
Large accounting platforms are natural bundlers.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed workflow-integration agreement granting least-privilege access to each accounting office's authorized KSeF workflows; unsigned
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Use sandbox demonstrations and serve individual SMEs through their own credentials; no production monitoring without authorization
critical_control_point.current_owner: Each taxpayer controls its KSeF permissions; accounting platforms control embedded workflows
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: Unknown today; proposed direct contracts with accounting offices
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: No present customer credentials or partner rights; founder can build against public KSeF documentation outside employer resources
critical_control_point.launch_controller: Prospective business after customer authorization, while taxpayers retain permission control
critical_control_point.subject: Authorized multi-client KSeF exception workflow

economics.acquisition_route: Build a read-only exception monitor, pilot with 2-3 independent accounting offices, then add guided resolution and SLA reporting
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Assumption: 300 offices at 1,200 PLN monthly yields 4.32m PLN ARR; at 25% owner earnings plus a 3-4x recurring-revenue equity value, retained equity and reinvested cash could exceed 5m PLN in roughly 5-8 years. Unknowns are churn, support intensity, and bundling.
economics.founder_time: 15-25 hours weekly during pilot, compatible with the 5-hour daily ceiling if support is scheduled and automated
economics.gross_margin_basis: Subscription revenue less cloud, document processing, and paid exception support; target 70%, unverified
economics.payback: Assumption: under 4 months on 2,000 PLN acquisition cost and 700 PLN monthly contribution; test required
economics.pricing: Assumption: 500-2,000 PLN monthly per office plus 2,000-6,000 PLN onboarding
economics.retention_or_repeat: Monthly while the office manages active taxpayers and exceptions

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: An anonymized library of failure patterns and resolution playbooks, subject to lawful data rights
fingerprint.customer: Polish accounting offices serving many SMEs
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Direct specialist outbound plus ERP referrals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Managed KSeF exception monitor sold as recurring software-enabled service
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Accounting-office owner pays when staff spend time resolving invoice exceptions
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Mandatory KSeF receipt and issuance shifts invoice handling into a new structured workflow

founder_fit: Data-science and automation skills fit exception classification and monitoring.
Can validate part-time with low capital and no camera-led distribution.
Polish location and language improve access to local accounting workflows.
risks: Platform vendors may bundle the feature.
Customer credentials and invoice data require strong security.

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: recurring multi client invoice exception operations
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: authorized accounting office ksef exception queue
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: continued ksef api and accounting system interoperability

structure.control_point: Authorized placement in an accounting office's exception queue

thesis: Mandatory KSeF adoption creates a narrow, measurable exception workload that a small Polish operator can automate before broad accounting suites perfect it.
title: KSeF Exception Desk for Accounting Offices
uncertainties: Exception frequency and labor cost per client are unknown.
Accounting-office willingness to grant access is unknown.
